en.title: The past perfect
en.summary: The past perfect shows that one past action came before another.

paragraphs: The past perfect describes an action that was already finished before another moment or action in the past. It is formed with had and the past participle, and it is the same for every person.

items: When I arrived, the film **had started**.
She **had already left** by the time he called.
I **had never seen** snow before that winter.

blocks.html:
FormExample
statementI had finished. She had finished.
questionHad you finished?
negativeHe had not (hadn't) finished.
short formI'd, you'd, she'd (also for would)

sections.title: The earlier of two past events

paragraphs: Use the past perfect for the earlier event and the simple past for the later one. This makes the order of events clear, even when the sentence does not follow the order they happened in.

blocks.html:
Order of eventsSentence
first: the film started; then: I arrivedWhen I arrived, the film had started.
first: she left; then: he calledShe had left when he called.
first: we ate; then: they cameWe had eaten before they came.

items: **by the time**: By the time we arrived, they had gone.
**after**, **before**: After he had eaten, he left.
**because**, **as**: She was tired because she had worked all night.
Wrong: **After I have eaten, I left.** Right: **After I had eaten, I left.**
Wrong: **She had went.** Right: **She had gone.**
Wrong: **I had seen him yesterday.** Right: **I saw him yesterday.** (use the past perfect only when it is the earlier of two past events)
